Proof:

By definition, the $p$-adic integers $\Z_p$ form the valuation ring induced by the $p$-adic norm $
orm{\cdot}_p$ on $\Q_p$. That is,
$$ \Z_p = \{x \in \Q_p \mid 
orm{x}_p \le 1\} $$

First, we determine the group of units of $\Z_p$. An element $x \in \Z_p$ is a unit if and only if there exists $y \in \Z_p$ such that $xy = 1$. 
If $x$ is a unit, then $
orm{x}_p \le 1$ and $
orm{x^{-1}}_p \le 1$. Since the norm is multiplicative, $
orm{x}_p 
orm{x^{-1}}_p = 
orm{1}_p = 1$. This implies $
orm{x}_p = 1$. 
Conversely, if $x \in \Z_p$ has $
orm{x}_p = 1$, then $x 
eq 0$, and its inverse $x^{-1} \in \Q_p$ satisfies $
orm{x^{-1}}_p = 1/
orm{x}_p = 1$, which means $x^{-1} \in \Z_p$.
Thus, the set of units in $\Z_p$, denoted $U$, is exactly $\{x \in \Q_p \mid 
orm{x}_p = 1\}$.

The set of non-units of $\Z_p$ is therefore
$$ M = \Z_p \setminus U = \{x \in \Q_p \mid 
orm{x}_p < 1\} $$

We will show that $M$ is an ideal of $\Z_p$. 
1. $0 \in M$ since $
orm{0}_p = 0 < 1$.
2. For any $x, y \in M$, the strong triangle inequality of the $p$-adic norm gives $
orm{x+y}_p \le \max(
orm{x}_p, 
orm{y}_p) < 1$. Thus, $x+y \in M$.
3. For any $x \in M$ and $r \in \Z_p$, the multiplicative property of the norm gives $
orm{rx}_p = 
orm{r}_p 
orm{x}_p \le 1 \cdot 
orm{x}_p = 
orm{x}_p < 1$. Thus, $rx \in M$.

Because $M$ is an ideal and contains all non-units of $\Z_p$, any proper ideal $I \subsetneq \Z_p$ can only contain non-units (if $I$ contained a unit, we would have $1 \in I$ and $I = \Z_p$). Thus, any proper ideal must be a subset of $M$. Consequently, $M$ is the unique maximal ideal of $\Z_p$. This proves part (a): $\Z_p$ is a local ring.

To prove part (b), we show that $M = p\Z_p$. 
For any $pz \in p\Z_p$ (where $z \in \Z_p$), we have $
orm{pz}_p = 
orm{p}_p 
orm{z}_p$. By the definition of the $p$-adic norm, $
orm{p}_p = 1/p$. Since $z \in \Z_p$, $
orm{z}_p \le 1$. Thus, $
orm{pz}_p \le 1/p < 1$, which means $pz \in M$. Therefore, $p\Z_p \subseteq M$.

Conversely, let $x \in M$. Then $
orm{x}_p < 1$. By the definition of the $p$-adic norm, its image on $\Q_p$ is the set $\{0\} \cup \{p^n \mid n \in \Z\}$. Since $
orm{x}_p < 1$ and $
orm{x}_p$ is either $0$ or a power of $p$, we must have $
orm{x}_p \le 1/p$. 
Consider the element $y = x/p \in \Q_p$. We have 
$$ 
orm{y}_p =  rac{
orm{x}_p}{
orm{p}_p} \le  rac{1/p}{1/p} = 1 $$
This implies that $y \in \Z_p$. Since $x = py$, we have $x \in p\Z_p$. 
Therefore, $M \subseteq p\Z_p$.

We conclude that $M = p\Z_p$. Since $M$ is the unique maximal ideal of $\Z_p$, the principal ideal $p\Z_p$ is the unique maximal ideal of $\Z_p$, proving part (b).
